expected_report.case_summary: 68M with Stage IIIA (pT2bN1M0) adenocarcinoma of left lower lobe s/p wedge resection. KRAS G12C+ , PD-L1 TPS 18%, EGFR wild-type. Adjuvant therapy indicated.
key_findings: Pathologically confirmed N1 disease (1/12 hilar node involved) → Stage IIIA post-resection
KRAS G12C mutation identified (targetable with sotorasib/adagrasib)
PD-L1 18% expression (below 50% threshold for single-agent checkpoint inhibition)
Negative margins, adequate lymph node sampling (12 nodes)
No distant metastases detected on imaging
expected_report.assessment: Patient with high-risk NSCLC (Stage IIIA, N1) requires adjuvant systemic therapy. KRAS G12C status opens potential for targeted approach.

recommendations.text: Adjuvant platinum-based doublet (platinum + pemetrexed for nonsquamous histology)
recommendations.details: 4 cycles recommended per NCCN Category 1 evidence. Expected median OS benefit ~10-15 months.

recommendations.text: Sequential or concurrent KRAS G12C inhibitor (sotorasib/adagrasib) following chemotherapy
recommendations.details: If available in local setting. CodeBreaK and KRYSTAL trials show benefit in metastatic KRAS-mutant NSCLC; adjuvant data emerging.

recommendations.text: Complete biomarker panel (MSI-H, TMB) for future surveillance/immunotherapy guidance
recommendations.details: Will help stratify recurrence risk and inform immunotherapy eligibility if progression occurs.

treatment_considerations.chemotherapy: Cisplatin 75 mg/m² + Pemetrexed 500 mg/m² every 3 weeks x 4 cycles
treatment_considerations.toxicity_monitoring: Baseline renal function, hearing (for cisplatin). Monitor for nausea, thrombocytopenia, neuropathy.
treatment_considerations.immunotherapy: Not recommended adjuvantly at this time; reserve for metastatic/recurrent disease

red_flags_and_uncertainties: 🚨 CRITICAL: Nodal involvement (N1) associated with 40-50% risk of distant recurrence even with adjuvant chemotherapy
⚠️ UNCERTAIN: Limited evidence for KRAS-targeted adjuvant therapy — recommend oncology consultation
⚠️ GAP: MSI-H and TMB not tested — would refine prognosis and guide future surveillance
next_steps: Refer to medical oncology for adjuvant chemotherapy planning
Confirm performance status (ECOG 0-1 required)
Baseline labs: CBC, CMP, LFTs, creatinine clearance
Baseline hearing assessment if cisplatin planned
Discuss KRAS-targeted therapy availability in region
Establish follow-up schedule (CT + labs every 3-6 months x 2-3 years)

expected_report.case_summary: 52F post-menopausal with cT2N1M0 (Stage IIIA) luminal HER2+ invasive ductal carcinoma, Grade 3. ER/PR+, HER2 IHC 3+ (FISH confirmed), Ki-67 65%. Neoadjuvant HER2-targeted + chemotherapy indicated.
key_findings: Hormone receptor co-expression (ER 90%, PR 75%) → Luminal HER2 subtype, high-risk
Grade 3 with high proliferation (Ki-67 65%) → Aggressive biology
Regional nodal involvement (cN1) → Locally advanced disease
expected_report.assessment: Locally advanced HER2+ breast cancer with favorable prognosis if treated adequately. Neoadjuvant dual HER2 targeting + chemotherapy is standard approach.

recommendations.details: Docetaxel 75 mg/m² + Trastuzumab (loading 8mg/kg then 6mg/kg) + Pertuzumab (loading 840mg then 420mg), all every 3 weeks x 4-6 cycles

recommendations.text: Cardiac monitoring before and during therapy (baseline echo/MUGA, repeat after 2 cycles)
recommendations.details: HER2-targeted therapy (especially dual targeting) carries ~8-10% risk of cardiac dysfunction. Ensure LVEF ≥50% before starting.

recommendations.text: Surgical resection 4-6 weeks after completing neoadjuvant therapy
recommendations.details: Breast-conserving surgery vs. mastectomy per patient preference and response. Sentinel lymph node ± axillary dissection based on residual disease.

recommendations.text: If pathologic complete response (pCR): Continue trastuzumab for 12 months total, add endocrine therapy (tamoxifen or AI) for 10 years
recommendations.details: pCR improves long-term outcomes significantly. Consider de-escalation if excellent response.

recommendations.text: If residual disease after neoadjuvant: Consider additional systemic therapy or clinical trial
recommendations.details: T-DM1 (ado-trastuzumab emtansine) or other CDCs under investigation in residual disease setting.

treatment_considerations.regimen: Docetaxel 75mg/m² + Trastuzumab + Pertuzumab IV every 3 weeks
treatment_considerations.cycles: 4-6 cycles depending on response and tolerability
treatment_considerations.toxicity_monitoring: Cardiac function (LVEF), CBC, nausea, peripheral neuropathy, hand-foot skin reaction (from taxane)
treatment_considerations.hormone_sensitivity: Patient is ER/PR+; adjuvant endocrine therapy is essential post-surgery

red_flags_and_uncertainties: 🚨 CRITICAL: Cardiac dysfunction risk with dual HER2 targeting — baseline echo mandatory
🚨 CRITICAL: High-grade, aggressive tumor — requires intensive systemic therapy
⚠️ NOTE: Grade 3 + Ki-67 65% suggests poor prognosis if undertreated; do not de-escalate without strong pCR
⚠️ POST-MENOPAUSAL: Will require endocrine therapy indefinitely (tamoxifen or letrozole/anastrozole + AI)
next_steps: Baseline cardiac assessment (echo, LVEF measurement, EKG)
Confirm performance status (ECOG 0-1)
Labs: CBC, CMP, LFTs, HER2 status confirmation
Multidisciplinary tumor board discussion (surgery, oncology, radiology)
Initiate neoadjuvant chemotherapy + trastuzumab + pertuzumab per above regimen
Restaging imaging (CT chest/abdomen/pelvis) after 2-3 cycles to assess response
Genetic counseling regarding BRCA negative status and implications

expected_report.case_summary: 61M with pT3N0M0 (Stage IIA) adenocarcinoma of descending colon s/p resection. MSI-HIGH, dMMR (MLH1/PMS2 loss) suggesting Lynch syndrome. BRAF wild-type.
key_findings: MSI-HIGH status confirmed (microsatellite instability on molecular testing)
Mismatch repair protein loss pattern (MLH1-, PMS2-) consistent with Lynch syndrome
BRAF wild-type (typical of Lynch syndrome, not sporadic MSI-H)
expected_report.assessment: Stage IIA CRC with MSI-H status. Prognosis is better than stage-matched MMR-proficient tumors. Adjuvant chemotherapy may be deferred in selected, compliant patients. Lynch syndrome workup essential.

recommendations.details: Stage IIA MSI-H disease has low recurrence risk (~10-15% vs. ~20-25% for MMR-proficient). Observation is Category 2B per NCCN.
recommendations.if_chosen: Patient must be counseled on recurrence risk and strict compliance with surveillance required

recommendations.text: Adjuvant chemotherapy with 5-FU or FOLFOX (4 cycles)
recommendations.details: If patient prefers treatment or has additional risk factors (high-grade, lymphovascular invasion, inadequate lymph node sampling). Benefit in MSI-H modest compared to MMR-proficient.
recommendations.if_chosen: Offers 2-5% recurrence risk reduction but with toxicity; patient preference crucial

recommendations.details: NOT recommended in adjuvant setting currently (NCCN). Reserve immunotherapy for metastatic/recurrent disease where benefit is clear.
recommendations.evidence_level: Standard (trials ongoing but not FDA-approved adjuvantly yet)

lynch_syndrome_workup.urgency: CRITICAL — MLH1/PMS2 loss pattern highly suspicious for Lynch syndrome
lynch_syndrome_workup.testing: Germline mismatch repair gene sequencing (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2, EPCAM)
lynch_syndrome_workup.family_implications: If confirmed, all first-degree relatives require genetic counseling and increased surveillance (colonoscopy every 2-3 years starting age 20-25)

surveillance_protocol_if_no_adjuvant: Colonoscopy: 1 year post-op, then every 3-5 years (or per Lynch protocol if confirmed)
Imaging (CT abdomen/pelvis ± chest): Every 6 months x 2-3 years, then annually
Labs (CEA): Consider baseline and at each imaging; trends may guide workup
Gynecologic screening if applicable (ovarian cancer risk elevated in Lynch)
surveillance_protocol_if_adjuvant_chosen: Same as above after chemotherapy completion
red_flags_and_uncertainties: 🚨 CRITICAL: Lynch syndrome pattern identified — germline testing MUST be arranged immediately
🚨 CRITICAL: Family members at risk — proband diagnosis must be communicated to relatives
⚠️ UNCERTAIN: T3N0 is borderline for adjuvant recommendation — patient preference paramount
⚠️ NOTE: MSI-H tumors have different biology; standard adjuvant chemotherapy benefit is reduced compared to MSI-stable CRC
next_steps: Urgent referral to medical oncology for treatment discussion (surveillance vs. adjuvant)
Arrange genetic counseling and germline mismatch repair testing
If Lynch confirmed: Notify patient's relatives, recommend their genetic evaluation
Establish surveillance schedule per NCCN CRC Guidelines (increased frequency for Lynch)
Baseline labs: CEA, LFTs, renal function
Patient education: Discuss options, recurrence risk, surveillance compliance, Lynch implications
Gynecologic/urologic screening per Lynch protocol if applicable
